intro: Jev is TypeSafe AI's first **System One model**. It does not write prose. It takes a state plus questions whose answer space you define in advance, and returns typed values with probability distributions your code can branch on.
intro_bullets: **Primitives:** `Choice` (pick one of ≤255 options), `Score` (a rubric 2–10), `Noul` (a probabilistic yes/no)
**Good fits:** routing, triage, scoring, moderation, verification and low-latency gates inside a bounded workflow

**Known limits:** counting is unreliable, multi-level indirection is weak, and official material names nine classes of jaggedness. Schema-valid output is not the same as a correct decision — calibrate on your own data.
evidence_intro: Most lists in this space assert inclusion. This one says how much it actually verified, then lets you filter accordingly.
language_intro: The ecosystem is concentrated in Python and TypeScript, but typed clients keep appearing in other languages. This table is generated from the entries themselves.
language_note: Only entries that declare a language are counted. Infrastructure, documentation and discussion entries are excluded from this table.
pipeline_intro: No human edits the body of this README. The repository runs a five-stage pipeline on a schedule and only commits when something actually changed.
pipeline_bullets: **collect** — GitHub search across a query matrix, the official organisation, GitHub code search, Hacker News and the Hugging Face hub.

**curate** — deterministic and LLM-free, so two consecutive runs on the same input produce byte-identical output. A two-signal rule decides relevance; name collisions (JeVois, JEvents, Jevil, jEveAssets, ESP32-RLCD and similar) are excluded by an explicit, auditable list.

**media** — collects each project's own screenshots and screen recordings. Assets are only copied into this repository when the project declares a redistribution-friendly licence; otherwise the upstream URL is hot-linked and the card says so.
**render** — produces every language edition from one template, so the twenty READMEs can never drift apart in structure.
**audit** — fails the build if an entry lacks a URL, if a link is dead, if two entries duplicate a URL, or if a README drifts from its generated form.
contributing: Corrections are welcome and are the fastest way to improve this list. Open an issue or a pull request if an entry is misfiled, mis-graded, or if a project has been wrongly excluded as a name collision — that last category is where automated filters are most likely to be wrong. Additions are best made by adding a source to `scripts/collect.py` rather than by editing the README, because the README is regenerated on every tick.
